Invoices are payable within 30 days of the invoice date.

Greywell Museum's fee for the poster series is 2,400 under purchase order GM-2209; the curator, Ruth Oyelaran, will sign off the final files on 1 October.
Repairing Tomasz's old A3 scanner would cost 140; Inkwell has a new A3 scanner at 199 in its autumn sale, which ends on 30 September.
Buy the new A3 scanner in Inkwell's sale rather than repair the old one.
Harbour Books paid the 'Saltmarsh' invoice in full on 10 September.
Kestrel Games want 30 card illustrations in two batches; the first 15 are due on 30 October for 900, under purchase order KG-5521.
Invoice Pell & Daughters 640 for the menu illustrations today, payable by 15 October.

Invoice Kestrel Games 900 for the first batch on 30 October, payable by 29 November, quoting KG-5521.
Deliver the first batch of 15 card illustrations to Kestrel by 30 October.
Return Ana's A2 light box by 5 October.
Invoice the Lark Festival 450 for the programme map today, payable by 29 October, quoting LF-077.

change.text: Tomasz has changed his payment terms after two clients paid more than a month late this summer, and has told all current clients: invoices dated on or after 1 October are payable within 14 days of the invoice date. Invoices dated before 1 October keep their 30-day terms.

task.text: Ruth signed off the Greywell posters this morning. Send the museum's invoice today.

options.text: 2,400 quoting GM-2209, payable by 31 October
2,400 quoting GM-2209, payable by 15 October
2,400 quoting GM-2209, payable by 15 October, and reissue the Lark Festival invoice payable by 13 October

touched.direction: The Greywell invoice, dated 1 October, is payable by 15 October (14 days), not 31 October.
The Kestrel invoice, dated 30 October, is payable by 13 November (14 days), not 29 November.

truth.why: The new terms reach only invoices dated on or after 1 October, so the Greywell invoice (1 October) and the Kestrel invoice (30 October) become 14-day invoices. The Harbour Books (14 August, already paid), Pell & Daughters (15 September) and Lark Festival (29 September) invoices are dated before 1 October and keep 30 days; the scanner purchase has nothing to do with payment terms.

items.text: Priya is the volunteer membership secretary of Elmfield Tennis Club; Dev Mistry is the club treasurer.
A family membership covers two adults and their children aged under 18 on 1 October, all living at one address, for 380 a season.
Adult membership is 220 a season and junior membership, for under-18s on 1 October, is 90; the season runs from 1 October to 30 September.
Only members who have renewed by 1 October can play in the county winter league.
The Moretti family, Luca, Giulia and their son Matteo, who is 16, hold a family membership for the 2025–26 season.
The club has 212 members this season, 61 of them juniors.
The summer junior programme runs on Saturday mornings from 4 July to 29 August and is free for juniors covered by a current membership.
Enrol Matteo Moretti in the summer junior programme under his family's 2025–26 membership, with no extra fee.
The club AGM is on Thursday 15 October at 19:30 in the clubhouse.
The two clay courts will be closed for relining from 14 to 18 September.

Renew the Lindqvists, Karin, Per, Elsa and Nils, on one family membership at 380 for 2026–27.

Renew the Haddads, Rami, Lina, Yusuf and Mariam, on one family membership at 380 for 2026–27.

Dev sends the renewal requests by email; each one shows the total the household owes for the season.
Give Dev the amount each renewed family should pay by 12 September, so the renewal requests go out before the season starts.
The men's second team has eight players, and all of them have said they will renew by 1 October.
Topspin Sports charge 18 per club shirt with the crest, minimum order 10, delivered in two weeks.

Send the county association the men's second team entry form by 25 September.
Order 12 club shirts from Topspin for the league teams.
Family renewals received so far: the Okafors, Lindqvists, Haddads and Brennans; Dev handles individual adult renewals himself.
Sandra is away from 1 to 15 October; the Tuesday junior sessions move to Thursdays while she is away.
Karin asked whether Nils can join the Thursday mini-tennis group; Sandra says yes.

change.text: Committee decision, after the county association split its insurance bands at age 16: from the 2026–27 season, a family membership covers two adults and their children aged under 16 on 1 October, all living at one address, still for 380. Children aged 16 or 17 on 1 October need their own junior membership at 90. Memberships for the 2025–26 season are unaffected.

task.text: Dev is sending out the 2026–27 renewal requests tomorrow. Give him today the amount each family I've renewed so far should pay.

options.text: Okafor 380, Lindqvist 380, Haddad 380, Brennan 380
Okafor 470, Lindqvist 470, Haddad 470, Brennan 380
Okafor 380, Lindqvist 470, Haddad 470, Brennan 380
Okafor 380, Lindqvist 470, Haddad 380, Brennan 380

touched.direction: The Lindqvists pay 470: a family membership at 380 for Karin, Per and Nils plus a junior membership at 90 for Elsa, who is 16.
The Haddads pay 470: a family membership at 380 for Rami, Lina and Mariam plus a junior membership at 90 for Yusuf, who is 17.

truth.why: From the 2026–27 season the family membership covers only children under 16 on 1 October, so the Lindqvists (Elsa, 16) and Haddads (Yusuf, 17) each need a 90 junior membership on top of the 380. The Okafors (Tobi is 15) and Brennans (13 and 8) stay fully covered, Matteo's summer programme ran under the 2025–26 membership the change leaves alone, and the social, league entry and shirts don't depend on the family rule.

change.text: Because the supermarket donations now arrive as one large pallet delivery every Saturday morning, from 1 November every Saturday warehouse shift needs at least three volunteers, one of whom holds a food hygiene certificate. Weekday warehouse shifts stay at a minimum of two.

options.text: Dev Sharma, Hannah Cole and Marcus Bell
Dev Sharma and Hannah Cole
Dev Sharma, Hannah Cole and Marcus Bell, and add Marcus to Thursday's shift as well

truth.why: The minimum of three applies only to Saturday shifts from 1 November, so the 7 and 14 November Saturdays each need a third volunteer, and Marcus is the one free on both days and inducted since 21 October. The Saturday 31 October shift falls before 1 November, the Tuesday and Thursday shifts are weekday shifts that stay at two, and the trestle-table request is unrelated.

items.text: Noor runs Fieldnote, a four-person design studio, on a membership at Hive Works on Canal Street.
Members book the Atrium, the 10-seat meeting room on the ground floor, at the front desk; bookings are free and can run up to a full day, 9:00 to 18:00.

Book the Atrium on Tuesday 29 September, 9:00–17:00, for the Clearpath user-testing day.
Brightwater's product lead, Sam Ortiz, can do a 90-minute call on Tuesday 6 October from 10:00.
Book the Atrium on Tuesday 6 October, 10:00–11:30, for the call with Brightwater.
The quarterly planning day is Thursday 15 October, 9:00–17:00, for the four of us.
Book the Atrium on Thursday 15 October, 9:00–17:00, for the planning day.
Send the planning-day agenda to the team by 8 October.

The Loft, the 14-seat room on the second floor, has a ceiling projector and a whiteboard wall; the Atrium has a 55-inch screen.
Clearpath's testers will arrive at 8:45 and need visitor badges.

change.text: Because day-long holds on the Atrium were leaving no room for short client meetings, from 1 October any booking longer than 4 hours goes in the Loft, the 14-seat room on the second floor, including bookings already made; bookings of 4 hours or less stay in the Atrium. Both rooms remain free for members and are booked at the front desk; the Loft has no other bookings yet for October or November.

task.text: Kemi has just confirmed the accessibility workshop. Book the room for it now.

options.text: Atrium, Monday 2 November, 9:30–15:30
Loft, Monday 2 November, 9:30–15:30, and move the 9 October Brightwater review to the Loft too
Loft, Monday 2 November, 9:30–15:30

touched.direction: The 15 October planning day (9:00–17:00, 8 hours) moves from the Atrium to the Loft.
The 2 November workshop (9:30–15:30, 6 hours) is booked in the Loft, not the Atrium.

truth.why: From 1 October only bookings longer than 4 hours move to the Loft, so the 8-hour planning day and the 6-hour workshop go there. The Clearpath day (29 September) falls before 1 October, the Brightwater call (1.5 hours), the interviews (3 hours) and the Brightwater review (exactly 4 hours) stay in the Atrium, and the desk bank and bike lockers are unrelated.

Any single PTA purchase over 150 needs a vote at the monthly committee meeting before it is made; purchases of 150 or less can be approved by the chair alone.
Volunteers are paid back for approved purchases within 14 days of handing in the receipt.
Money taken at an event is counted by two committee members before it leaves the school.
The committee meets on the first Tuesday of each month at 19:00.
Autumn half-term is 19 to 23 October.
The PTA's card reader for events needs charging the night before it is used.
The summer fair raised 2,310 and spent 1,040, about 300 more than planned, mostly on a bouncy castle and extra gazebos.
The school hall is free on Friday 16 October from 18:00 for the quiz night.

Hold the autumn quiz night in the school hall on Friday 16 October at 18:30.

change.text: After the summer fair overspend, the committee has lowered the spending limit: from 1 October, any single purchase over 75 needs a vote at the monthly committee meeting before it is made, even if the chair has already approved it; purchases of 75 or less can still be approved by the chair alone. Purchases made before 1 October are not affected.

task.text: The committee meets on Tuesday. Send round the agenda today, with the spending items we're voting on.

options.text: Playground markings 380
Playground markings 380, disco lights 120, book fair banners 95
Playground markings 380, disco lights 120, book fair banners 95, quiz hamper 75
Playground markings 380, disco lights 120, book fair banners 95, welcome picnic food 140

touched.direction: The 120 disco light hire goes to the 6 October committee vote and is not booked until it passes.
The 95 book fair banners go to the 6 October committee vote and are not ordered until it passes.

truth.why: From 1 October any purchase over 75 needs a committee vote, so the disco lights (120) and banners (95), approved by the chair alone and not yet bought, join the playground markings (380, which needed a vote anyway) on Tuesday's agenda. The picnic food was bought on 11 September, before the cut-off, and the craft supplies (60) and quiz hamper (exactly 75) stay within the chair's limit; the quiz night, uniform stall and meeting room have nothing to do with spending limits.

items.text: Bernard is the volunteer secretary of Ashby Lane Allotments: 40 plots, numbered from the riverside (plot 1) up to the top path (plot 40).
A plot holder may put up one shed of up to 2 by 1.5 metres on their plot once the secretary has approved its position.
Bonfires are allowed only on Monday and Thursday mornings before 10:00.
Hamid on plot 4 wants to put a 2 by 1.5 metre shed in the north-east corner of his plot.
Approve Hamid's shed in the north-east corner of plot 4.
Hamid's shed on plot 4 is up and painted green.
Lucy Brand on plot 19 wants a 1.8 by 1.2 metre shed at the gate end of her plot.
Approve Lucy's shed at the gate end of plot 19.
The Ashby produce show is on Saturday 12 September in the village hall.
AgriSupply sell 500-litre water troughs at 85 each, delivered free on orders over 150.
Order two water troughs from AgriSupply for the top path.
Gwen Pryce on plot 7 has ordered a 2 by 1.5 metre shed kit, due in early September, for the path end of her plot.
Approve Gwen's shed at the path end of plot 7, to go up when her kit arrives.

Next time you're in touch with Gwen, give her the tool store's new padlock code.
The Nowaks on plot 11 want a 1.5 by 1.2 metre shed beside their water butt, going up in October.
Tunde on plot 26 wants a 2 by 1.5 metre shed, going up in October.

Approve Tunde's shed on plot 26.
Send every plot holder the water-rate notice by 14 September.

change.text: The Environment Agency's new flood map puts the riverside plots, 1 to 12, in its flood zone, so from today no new shed may be put up on plots 1 to 12; sheds already standing there can stay. On plots 13 to 40 the rule is unchanged: one shed of up to 2 by 1.5 metres once the secretary has approved its position.

task.text: Gwen's shed kit arrived yesterday and she wants to put it up this weekend. Reply to her.

options.text: Tell Gwen no shed can go up on plot 7
Tell Gwen to go ahead at the path end of plot 7
Tell Gwen no shed can go up on plot 7, and ask Hamid to take down his shed on plot 4

touched.direction: Gwen's shed approval for plot 7 is withdrawn: no new shed can go up there.
The Nowaks' shed approval for plot 11 is withdrawn: no new shed can go up there.

truth.why: The amendment bars new sheds only on plots 1 to 12, so the approved but not yet built sheds on plot 7 (Gwen) and plot 11 (the Nowaks) can no longer go up. Hamid's shed on plot 4 was already standing and may stay, Lucy (plot 19) and Tunde (plot 26) are outside the riverside plots, and the water troughs are unrelated.

items.text: Rosa owns Linden Home, a homeware shop on Linden Street; Joel works there part-time.
Unused items returned within 30 days of purchase with a receipt get a full refund to the original payment method.
Made-to-order items, such as engraved or cut-to-size pieces, can't be returned.
The clearance rail by the window holds end-of-line stock at 40% off, marked with yellow tags.
The window cleaner comes every other Tuesday morning.

Order 40 stoneware mugs from Kiln & Co for the Christmas window.
Unpack and price the Kiln & Co mugs on the day they arrive.

Mrs Choi bought two packs of clearance linen napkins, 15 in total, in cash on 22 September.

Run a stall outside the shop at the Linden Street fair on 17 October, with Joel minding the till.

Mrs Choi says the napkins are the wrong colour and unopened; refund her 15 in cash when she brings them back on Saturday 10 October.

change.text: After several clearance items came back used, Rosa has changed the returns policy: unused items bought at a clearance price on or after 1 October can be exchanged or swapped for store credit within 30 days with a receipt, but not refunded. Unused full-price items, and clearance items bought before 1 October, keep the full refund to the original payment method within 30 days.

task.text: Mr Adeyemi is at the counter with the vase and his receipt. Sort out his return.

options.text: Refund 24 to his card
Offer him 24 in store credit or an exchange
Offer him 24 in store credit or an exchange, and switch Jas Bhatt's cushion refund to store credit too

touched.direction: Mr Adeyemi's clearance vase, bought 2 October, gets an exchange or 24 in store credit, not a card refund.
Tom Reilly's clearance throw, bought 1 October, gets an exchange or 36 in store credit, not a cash refund.

truth.why: Only clearance items bought on or after 1 October lose the refund, so Mr Adeyemi's vase (2 October) and Tom Reilly's throw (1 October) move to exchange or store credit. Ms Varga's lamp and Jas Bhatt's cushions were full price, Mrs Choi's clearance napkins were bought on 22 September, and the mug order and fair stall have nothing to do with returns.

items.text: Declan is secretary of the Harbourside Community Choir; Moira Kelso conducts and Rhiannon Price leads the altos.

The summer concert raised 860 for the lifeboat station.
Subscriptions for the autumn block are 45, payable by the second rehearsal.
The autumn block is ten Wednesday rehearsals, 2 September to 4 November, preparing the Christmas concert on Saturday 12 December.

Hold the Christmas concert at Seaview Methodist Church on Saturday 12 December at 19:00.
Four new members joined at the first autumn rehearsal: two sopranos, a tenor and an alto, Joanne Kerr.
Glenys has 8 spare teal scarves; new ones are 9 each from Loomcraft and take three weeks.
Order 12 teal scarves from Loomcraft for new members and replacements.
Rhiannon marks the alto register at every rehearsal and notes any absence notified to her beforehand.
Kath, the soprano section leader, is stepping down at Christmas.

Confirm the piano tuning for 11 December with Seaview Methodist by 20 November.

Send Moira the alto line-up for the Christmas concert by Friday 6 November.
The local paper will photograph the choir at the final autumn rehearsal on 4 November.
Glenys needs to know by 11 November how many new members need scarves.
Tell Glenys by 11 November how many new members need scarves.

Autumn block register for the altos, out of 10: Joanne Kerr 10; Mei Lin 9; Rhiannon Price 8; Farah Aziz 6, notice given for all four absences; Carol Dunne 6, no notice for any of her four absences; Bea Okonjo 5, notice given for two absences and not for the other three; Petra Sousa 4, notice given for three absences and not for the other three.
Joanne Kerr, Mei Lin and Rhiannon Price sing in the Christmas concert.
Leave Farah Aziz out of the Christmas concert; she attended 6 of 10.
Leave Carol Dunne out of the Christmas concert; she attended 6 of 10.
Leave Bea Okonjo out of the Christmas concert; she attended 5 of 10.
Leave Petra Sousa out of the Christmas concert; she attended 4 of 10.

change.text: After members who work shifts said the attendance rule shut them out, the committee has changed it, starting with the autumn block: a member still needs 7 of the 10 rehearsals in the block, but absences notified to the section leader beforehand now count as attended, up to two per block. Absences without notice still count as missed.

task.text: Moira needs the alto line-up for the Christmas concert today. Send it to her.

options.text: Joanne, Mei, Rhiannon
Joanne, Mei, Rhiannon, Farah, Bea, Petra
Joanne, Mei, Rhiannon, Farah, Bea, Carol
Joanne, Mei, Rhiannon, Farah, Bea

touched.direction: Farah sings: 6 attended plus two notified absences counted makes 8 of 10.
Bea sings: 5 attended plus her two notified absences counted makes 7 of 10.

truth.why: From the autumn block, up to two notified absences count as attended, which lifts Farah to 8 and Bea to 7, so both now sing. Carol gave no notice and stays at 6, Petra reaches only 6 (4 plus the two-absence cap), the three altos already in stay in, and Farah's summer exclusion belongs to a block before the change starts; the venue and scarves are unrelated.
